lesson.title: The data protection officer
lesson.summary: Decide whether a data protection officer is mandatory, and protect the role's independence.

prerequisites.reason: The DPO cooperates with and is the contact for the supervisory authority.
The DPO is designated by, and advises, the controller or processor.
One mandatory-DPO case is large-scale special-category data.

blocks: A **data protection officer** (DPO) must be designated where (Article 37(1)):

items: (a) processing is carried out by a **public authority** or body, except courts acting in their judicial capacity;
(b) the **core activities** consist of processing that requires **regular and systematic monitoring** of people on a **large scale**; or
(c) the **core activities** consist of **large-scale** processing of special-category or criminal-offence data.

blocks: In other cases, appointing a DPO is voluntary, **unless EU or national law requires it** (Article 37(4)).
Some countries add their own requirements. This course does not cover national law, so check yours.

The DPO must have **expert knowledge** of data protection law and practice (Article 37(5)). The DPO may be a staff member or work under a service contract (Article 37(6)). A group of companies may share one DPO if the DPO is easily accessible from each establishment (Article 37(2)).
The DPO's contact details must be published and given to the supervisory authority (Article 37(7)).

items: involved properly and in good time in all data protection issues;
receives **no instructions** about how to perform their tasks;
**not dismissed or penalised** for performing them;
reports directly to the **highest management level**;
may hold other roles only if there is no conflict of interests.

blocks: **Tasks** (Article 39(1)): to inform and advise the organisation and its staff; to **monitor compliance**, including training and audits; to advise on data protection impact assessments (DPIAs); to **cooperate with the supervisory authority** and act as its contact point.
People may contact the DPO about their data and rights (Article 38(4)).
Sunfield's core activity is baking and selling bread. Its staff and customer processing supports that, but it is not obviously large-scale monitoring or large-scale sensitive-data processing.
So a DPO may not be mandatory under Article 37(1). National law may still require one under Article 37(4), and Sunfield must check.

blocks.text: These Sunfield examples are **illustrations**. A real assessment depends on all the facts.
